title: The guards karta only ran on Claude Code now run on Codex too
summary: Codex CLI's hooks surface is stable and on by default (stable since 0.124.0, plugin hooks loading since 0.131.0), so three karta guards that had no Codex home — the advisory that names a worker which produced nothing, the status summary at session start, and the two fail-closed checks on a review dispatch — ship as Codex twins alongside the three already bundled. The compatibility page stops promising doctrine where code now enforces, adds the row it never had, and replaces a feature-flag warning that no longer describes any Codex build.
motivation: Codex hooks are stable and on by default since 0.124.0 ("Hooks are now stable"), with plugin hooks enabled since 0.131.0, so three rules karta could only state in prose on Codex are now enforceable there, and the parity table is describing a hook surface that no longer exists.

design_facts.stack: Claude Code + Codex CLI plugin repo: markdown skills, stdlib-Python guard scripts and validators

included: .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/guard_subagent_whiff.py — a new hand-maintained Codex twin of the SubagentStop whiff advisory: the same git-fact detection, the same narrowing to karta-typed subagents, the stop_hook_active loop guard, both Codex block channels, and fail-open on every internal error

.codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/inject_karta_status.py — a new hand-maintained Codex twin of the SessionStart status injection: the same one-line-per-binder summary, the same inert fence and closing-marker neutralization, the same 10-line and 4096-byte budget, the same fail-open Karta Watch ensure, emitted on the channel Codex documents for session context, always exit 0

.codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/guard_auditor_dispatch.py and .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/guard_gate_dispatch.py — new hand-maintained Codex twins of the two fail-closed dispatch inspectors, registered on Codex's agent-dispatch PreToolUse event, denying with exit 2 and the reason on stderr and with the documented JSON deny decision on stdout

.codex-plugin/hooks/hooks.json and .codex/hooks.json — the bundled manifest and the repo-local manifest each gain the SubagentStop, SessionStart and agent-dispatch entries, in the fail-open launcher idiom the file already uses, and each description grows to name the guards it now carries
plugins/karta/.codex-plugin/** — the Codex install projection, regenerated by uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py after every .codex-plugin edit and never hand-edited

docs/how-to/codex.md — the parity table after the port: the two dispatch rows and the session-start row flip to enforced-bundled, a whiff-advisory row is added where the table had none, the Karta Watch revival row records that a Codex SessionStart hook now exists, and the stale feature-flag caveat is replaced by the generally-available facts
excluded: The writer-confinement guard is not ported. karta registers no kaizen or doc-gardner writer on Codex, so there is no writer for a confinement hook to recognize; that parity row stays doctrine and is left as written

hooks/hooks.json and every Claude guard under hooks/scripts/ are unchanged. This binder adds a second implementation of an existing rule; it never edits the rule or the surface that already enforces it

benchmarks/flow/mutation-surface.json and its rendered matrix are untouched. Two of its Codex rows will read stale once these twins ship, but that manifest's headline count is pinned to a named manifest_version, so re-statusing rows moves a benchmark denominator and belongs to a release-time bench pass with its own probe re-run
No new dependency anywhere: every twin is pure stdlib, like the three Codex guards it joins
The repo's .codex/rules/karta.rules execpolicy and the git-commit gate adapter (scripts/hooks/codex_precommit_gate.py) are unchanged
No skill, agent, or generated skill projection changes. The only generated files this binder rewrites are the plugins/karta/.codex-plugin/ copies of the hook assets

work_items.title: A Codex worker that produced nothing gets named instead of vanishing
work_items.summary: Port the subagent-stop whiff advisory to Codex so a karta-typed subagent stopping over stranded work is told once to name it in its report.
work_items.contract: NEW FILE .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/guard_subagent_whiff.py — a canonical, HAND-MAINTAINED Codex twin of hooks/scripts/guard_subagent_whiff.py, in the mold of the three twins already in that directory. It is not generated and is never compared byte-for-byte with the Claude original: same rule, different payload shape. Executable bit set. (1) SIGNAL — identical to the Claude twin, deterministic git facts only, never prose. A finding is a live-binder work item (binders read the way guard_delivery_stop.py reads them: .karta/binders/*.json in the working tree or in HEAD, never archive/) where ALL hold: no ref of any state stands under refs/karta/<slug>/item-<id>/; the item branch karta/<slug>/item-<id> exists and its tip is an ancestor of the integration tip — the tip of the integration branch karta/<slug>/integration, resolved exactly as the Claude original resolves it —, so the branch contributes no commits; and the branch is not checked out in a worktree with visible uncommitted work. Every exclusion errs toward silence, exactly as the original documents: a standing ref of any state, a branch carrying commits, a missing integration branch, an unreadable binder, and a dirty worktree all drop the item. (2) IDENTITY NARROWING — the guard fires only when the stopping subagent's own identity is karta-typed: a bare karta-* name or a plugin-scoped *:karta-* form, prefix-matched. Read that identity from the Codex SubagentStop payload; the docs ground this today: Codex hook input documents optional top-level agent_type and agent_id fields, so the twin reads agent_type ONLY (keeping the Claude twin's key) — agent_id is an opaque identifier, not a type, and is NEVER used to infer identity: typing from an id would be circumstance, not content. The build worker re-verifies the field names against the live hooks page, best-effort: the grounded facts here govern when the page is unreachable from the isolated worktree. The docs also state plain text output is invalid for stop events, so the stdout form is the JSON block decision. A payload with no identity field passes. A non-karta stop takes a payload-only fast path with ZERO subprocess calls. (3) LOOP GUARD — stop_hook_active true passes. No sentinel file and no state of any kind: the harness flag is the block-once, and a later karta-typed stop over the same residue is nudged again by design. (4) CHANNELS — on a finding emit BOTH forms Codex documents, as .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/guard_delivery_stop.py already does for Stop: the JSON block decision on stdout and the same reason on stderr with exit 2. Whichever the host honors, the subagent is turned back once. The nudge text keeps the Claude twin's content: name the stranded items, state the git facts asserted, say that a wave-mate still setting up can look identical and the orchestrator's frontier re-derivation disambiguates, and say the advisory fires once. (5) POSTURE — ADVISORY and FAIL-OPEN: a pass emits nothing on stdout — the JSON decision appears only on a finding; any internal error exits 0; an unreadable payload, missing fields, a non-git cwd, and a git-absent host all pass. A stray stop trap is worse than a missed nudge. (6) RESOLUTION — if the twin resolves any plugin-relative path, use the idiom the other twins use: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT first, then this script's own plugin root derived from __file__. (7) SELF-TEST — a --self-test mode that runs as CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=<repo> python3 .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/guard_subagent_whiff.py --self-test, exits 0/1, and prints a final summary of the exact form 'N/N checks passed' with N at least 10 — the oracle parses it and rejects a lower floor. Scope reference, not a quota: the Claude original's self-test carries 32 cases. Cover at minimum the Codex payload shape, the karta-typed and non-karta identity paths, the stop_hook_active pass, each documented exclusion, both emitted channels, and the fail-open paths. (8) BOTH MANIFESTS gain a SubagentStop entry: .codex-plugin/hooks/hooks.json in its bundled ${PLUGIN_ROOT} fail-open launcher idiom, .codex/hooks.json in its repo-local git rev-parse --show-toplevel fail-open launcher idiom. A launcher may additionally consult CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, which Codex sets for compatibility, but the fail-open shape must survive: an unresolved root allows rather than wedging the session. The group's matcher must be match-all - the documented spellings are "*", the empty string, or omitting the field, and the shipped manifests use "*" - because Codex applies a SubagentStop matcher to the agent_type: any narrower value silently disables the guard, whose identity filtering happens in-process. Each file's description grows to name this guard. (9) AFTER THE EDIT run uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py so plugins/karta/.codex-plugin/ regenerates; never hand-edit the projection. SURFACING NOTE — this item is expected to flag the sensitive-zone signal and the contract signal, and the flags are pre-justified here: it registers a new guard on an enforcement surface, and it consumes an event name and payload shape this repo does not own. Neither is an unresolved question about the rule, which is settled and copied.

work_items.title: A Codex session opens knowing which binders are in flight
work_items.summary: Port the session-start status summary to Codex so a session begins with a short, fenced line per live binder instead of nothing.
work_items.contract: NEW FILE .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/inject_karta_status.py — a canonical, HAND-MAINTAINED Codex twin of hooks/scripts/inject_karta_status.py. Not generated, never byte-compared with the Claude original. Executable bit set. (1) JOB — on the Codex session-start event, emit at most one short line per binder found at <cwd>/.karta/binders/*.json: slug, item count, pinned packs. Prefer the karta-status derivation script skills/karta-status/scripts/karta_next.py --json for live status and the next action, resolved via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT with a fallback that finds this script's own plugin root from __file__ by EXISTENCE TEST — walk parent directories until one actually contains the skills/ tree — never a fixed parent depth copied from the Claude original, whose directory sits one level shallower; degrade to a static binder summary when it is not invocable — the static-degrade path is a sanctioned outcome; degradation also applies when the derivation script resolves and runs but exits non-zero or emits unusable output. The oracle's temp-directory probe holds on either path — its assertions are path-independent — and the live path is covered by self-test fixtures. Silence when there are no binders. (2) BUDGETS — total output stays within 10 lines including the fence pair and within 4096 bytes; on overflow the body detail lines are trimmed, never the fence and never the appended watch line or its key material. (3) FENCE — wrap the block in the inert <karta-status> ... </karta-status> delimiter pair and carry over the closing-marker neutralization verbatim in behavior: the literal marker, escaped-slash spellings, HTML entities, URL encoding, and variants interleaved with Unicode format characters are all defanged before wrapping, and the inert replacement itself carries no escape sequence. Binder slugs are attacker-writable repo text, so this is a security boundary, not formatting. (4) KARTA WATCH — fire the same fail-open, fire-and-forget serve_status.py --ensure, and append the single watch line only when the current repo is opted in per the per-user watch store: the URL banner when the hub answers, the one-line revive nudge when it does not, with the same short re-probe before nudging. A repo that is not opted in produces the same output it would have produced without the watch feature and pays only a stat and read of the small state JSON. A Codex sandbox may deny the detached spawn; the ensure fails open and the nudge line covers it. (5) CHANNEL — emit the injected context on the channel Codex documents for session start. The docs ground this today: two documented FORMS exist — "Plain text on stdout is added as extra developer context" and the hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext JSON field — and they are alternative encodings of the SAME stdout stream, not two channels; the Stop twin's both-channels precedent pairs stdout with stderr and does not transfer here. Emit the PLAIN-STDOUT form ONLY: the fenced block as bare text, never a JSON wrapper and never both concatenated (concatenation would corrupt a JSON-parsing host and double-inject on a text-reading one). The build worker re-verifies the two forms against the live hooks page, best-effort: the grounded facts here govern when the page is unreachable from the isolated worktree. The handler caps injected context at additionalContextLimit (default 2500 tokens); the twin's own 10-line/4096-byte budget keeps typical output well under it, a host configured lower may truncate the tail, and containment does not depend on the closing fence arriving — the neutralization rewrites the CONTENT, so a truncated block degrades formatting, never safety. Plain stdout must stay a valid emission path so the behavioral probe below is meaningful. (6) POSTURE — informational and FAIL-OPEN: ALWAYS exit 0. A status hint must never surface as a session error, an unreadable payload exits 0, and an unresolvable karta_next degrades rather than failing. (7) SELF-TEST — a --self-test mode that runs as CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=<repo> python3 .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/inject_karta_status.py --self-test, exits 0/1, and prints a final summary of the exact form 'N/N checks passed' with N at least 10 — the oracle parses it and rejects a lower floor. Scope reference, not a quota: the Claude original's self-test carries 38 cases. Cover at minimum the no-binders silence, the one-line-per-binder shape, every neutralization spelling the original covers, both budget trims, the opted-in and not-opted-in watch paths, and the always-exit-0 rule on its error paths too: an unreadable payload, a malformed binder JSON, and a non-git cwd each exit 0. (8) BOTH MANIFESTS gain a SessionStart entry: .codex-plugin/hooks/hooks.json in its bundled ${PLUGIN_ROOT} fail-open launcher idiom, .codex/hooks.json in its repo-local git rev-parse --show-toplevel fail-open launcher idiom; a launcher may additionally consult CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, which Codex sets for compatibility, provided the fail-open shape survives. The group's matcher must be match-all ("*", empty, or omitted - the shipped manifests use "*"): Codex applies a SessionStart matcher to the start source, so a narrower value silently stops the injection for the sources it excludes. Each file's description grows to name this hook and to say it informs and never blocks. (9) AFTER THE EDIT run uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py. SURFACING NOTE — the expected flags are pre-justified: this hook writes repo-derived text into a model's context, which is the sensitive zone, and it spawns a detached process, which is a capability the sandbox may deny. Neither is an open question about the rule.

work_items.title: A review dispatch on Codex is refused when it is missing what the reviewer needs
work_items.summary: Port both fail-closed dispatch inspectors to Codex so a gate or auditor dispatch without its binder, its checklists, or a real sized diff is denied before two reviewer contexts spin up.
work_items.contract: TWO NEW FILES, .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/guard_auditor_dispatch.py and .codex-plugin/hooks/scripts/guard_gate_dispatch.py — canonical, HAND-MAINTAINED Codex twins of the same-named Claude guards. Not generated, never byte-compared with the originals. Both executable. They ship together because they share the dispatch-payload parsing, the recognition key set, and the manifest matcher. (1) MATCHER — the build worker CONFIRMS the live Codex agent-dispatch tool name against the published Codex hooks documentation (developers.openai.com/codex/hooks); the docs ground this today: the dispatch tool_name is spawn_agent and the docs state the matcher alias "spawn_agent also matches Agent" (matchers are regex strings), so the manifest matcher is spawn_agent|Agent unless the live page has moved. The dispatch tool_input carries message and task_name with an optional agent_type (a field set grounded in the Codex source, codex-rs multi_agents_v2 spawn.rs, because the docs leave tool_input unsettled) — so both guards join message and task_name into the inspected text alongside the Claude originals' prompt/description keys, and the build worker re-verifies tool name, alias, and field set against the live hooks page before writing the matcher — best-effort: if the page is unreachable from the isolated worktree, or disagrees with these grounded facts, build on the grounded facts recorded here and note the divergence in the item report; the oracle pins spawn_agent, and a real upstream rename is a binder amendment, not a silent matcher change. (2) RECOGNITION — neither guard keys on the tool name; both read the agent identity out of the payload's tool_input, exactly as the Claude originals do, so a matcher change never silently disarms them. Keep the originals' key set (subagent_type, agent_type, agent, agent_name, name) — agent_type is the documented Codex dispatch identity field — and ALSO test task_name, because a bare Codex plugin install dispatches gates through a generic fallback agent whose only karta-bearing content is the task label, and Codex task names conventionally use underscores: recognition therefore accepts both spellings, karta-safety-auditor and karta_safety_auditor (likewise karta-acceptance-reviewer / karta_acceptance_reviewer), in any of those identity fields. Recognition is a substring test on those FIELDS only — deliberately as broad as the Claude originals', because an over-match costs one bounded deny with a clear reason while an under-match silently disarms the gate: guard_auditor_dispatch recognizes the safety auditor; guard_gate_dispatch recognizes either gate. A prose mention of an agent inside message/prompt text is NOT recognition. STATED LIMIT (feeds the parity-table item): a fallback dispatch that carries a generic agent_type and no karta-bearing task_name is not recognized — the enforced claim in the docs is scoped to dispatches that identify their gate in a payload identity field. (3) AUDITOR RULE — identical to the Claude original. For a recognized dispatch, the joined prompt and description text must name a binder path matching .karta/binders/<slug>.json; that binder must load as JSON, resolved against the payload cwd for a relative path; and when the binder pins a non-empty sme[] the text must carry resolved checklist evidence — rule-id item lines of the form '- [ ] <prefix>.<n> — ', or rule-id tokens appearing after the word checklist. Missing binder path, unresolvable or unparseable binder, or pinned packs with no checklist evidence each DENY, with the original's reason text carried over (the auditor cannot re-derive built-in packs, which live in the plugin and not the worktree). (4) GATE RULE — identical to the Claude original. For a recognized dispatch the text must carry a parseable <rev>..<rev> or <rev>...<rev> range token (three-dot form split first, endpoint characters as the original defines them so a tag like v1.17.0 is not mis-split); the range must resolve and must NOT be empty; and a 'Diff-size: <files> files, <bytes> bytes' line must be present with numbers matching what git recomputes for that range — and a mismatch deny NAMES the recomputed numbers in its reason using the verbatim fragment 'recomputes Diff-size: <files> files, <bytes> bytes' — the reason may also echo the claimed numbers, but the recomputed pair rides that exact fragment, so a probe (and a human) can correct the dispatch from the denial alone without guessing which pair is which. The literal 'Diff-size:' is verbatim and case-sensitive. Worktree resolution follows the original's mention rule, including that a malformed worktree mention DENIES rather than falling back to the payload cwd. Missing range, unresolvable range, empty range, missing Diff-size line, and mismatched Diff-size numbers each deny. (5) DENY CHANNELS — emit BOTH forms Codex documents: on stdout the exact JSON shape {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "deny", "permissionDecisionReason": <reason>}}, and the same reason on stderr with exit 2 — one reason, two channels, byte for byte, following the both-channels precedent the Codex Stop twin already sets. (6) POSTURE — FAIL-CLOSED on the recognized shape ONLY, as the originals are: an internal error while checking a RECOGNIZED dispatch denies with a reason that names what to re-dispatch with; an unreadable payload, a payload with no tool_input dict, a non-dispatch payload, and an unrecognized dispatch shape all pass with exit 0. STATE THIS EXPLICITLY IN EACH DOCSTRING because it is the subtle part: the manifest LAUNCHER is fail-open and the GUARD is fail-closed, and they are not in conflict — the launcher only decides whether the guard runs at all when the plugin root does not resolve, while the fail-closed rule governs once the guard is running. Neither posture may be traded for the other. (7) RESOLUTION — plugin-relative lookups use CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT first, then this script's own plugin root derived from __file__. (8) SELF-TESTS — each script exposes --self-test, runnable as CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=<repo> python3 <script> --self-test, exiting 0/1 and printing a final summary of the exact form 'N/N checks passed' with N at least 10 per script — the oracle parses it and rejects a lower floor. Scope reference, not a quota: the Claude originals carry 13 and 37 cases. Cover at minimum every deny reason above, the unrecognized-shape passes, the prose-mention non-recognition, both emitted deny channels, and the fail-closed internal-error path. (9) BOTH MANIFESTS gain a PreToolUse group whose matcher is the confirmed dispatch tool name and whose hooks launch both guards — .codex-plugin/hooks/hooks.json in its bundled ${PLUGIN_ROOT} fail-open launcher idiom, .codex/hooks.json in its repo-local git rev-parse --show-toplevel fail-open launcher idiom; a launcher may additionally consult CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, which Codex sets for compatibility, provided the fail-open shape survives. Each file's description grows to name both guards and to record the launcher-open / guard-closed split. (10) AFTER THE EDIT run uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py. SURFACING NOTE — the expected flags are pre-justified: two fail-closed guards land on the review path, and the tool name and payload field names are an external interface. The one genuine open question, the live dispatch tool name, is carried as its own signal and is closed by the confirmation step in item (1) rather than guessed here.

work_items.contract: EDIT docs/how-to/codex.md only. Nothing here changes code; this item makes the page match the three items that did. 'Safety-auditor dispatch is complete' and 'Gate dispatches carry a real, sized diff' each lose their 'Doctrine for now' Codex cell and gain a cell that begins with the verbatim label 'Enforced (bundled Codex hook)' — the exact phrase the oracle checks — then states the rule in the same voice the other enforced rows use, INCLUDING the recognition scope the inspectors actually have: the guard recognizes a dispatch that identifies its gate in a payload identity field (agent_type, or a karta-bearing task name in either spelling); a bare plugin install's generic fallback dispatch that names neither is outside the enforced claim — a dispatch missing its binder or its checklists, and a dispatch with an empty diff range or a missing or mismatched Diff-size line, are denied before the reviewers spin up — and stating that this is live only after the per-user trust review. (2) FLIP the 'You see your binders at session start' row from 'Not shipped' to a cell beginning with the verbatim label 'Enforced (bundled Codex hook)' that names the SessionStart injection, keeping the honest qualifier that it informs and never blocks and adding that it fails open. (3) ADD a row the table has never had, for the whiff advisory: a plain-language rule label (the work a subagent produced nothing for is named, not lost), a Claude cell recording the plugin SubagentStop advisory, and a Codex cell recording the bundled Codex SubagentStop twin with the same block-once-then-pass behavior the stop_hook_active flag gives it. The Codex cell must contain the literal string SubagentStop and must be the ONLY Codex cell in the table that does. (4) UPDATE the 'Karta Watch hub auto-revives' row: its Codex cell currently explains that revival rides the script because the hooks surface is gated per user and off on some builds. Rewrite it so it says a bundled Codex SessionStart hook now exists and fires the same ensure once trusted, that the script-embedded ensure remains the path that always runs, and keep the sandbox caveat and the serve_status.py --ensure call to action unchanged in substance. (5) UPDATE the paragraph introducing that section so the sentence enumerating the bundled guards names the ones now bundled rather than the older three — and the page, taken as a whole, names every bundled Codex guard script by filename, the three existing and the four this binder adds, which the oracle checks one filename at a time. (6) REPLACE the first bullet of 'Before you rely on it'. The bullet titled 'Hooks may be off on your build' and its sentence about a feature flag on some builds go. In their place, state as facts: Codex hooks are stable and on by default since 0.124.0 (release note: "Hooks are now stable"), with plugin hooks enabled since 0.131.0; the off switch is the config line [features] hooks = false; trust is hash-based, so plugin and project hooks enforce only after the user reviews them through /hooks; and hosted tools fire no hooks, so a guard sees local function tools only. Keep the existing per-user-trust bullet and the hosted-tools sentence coherent with the rewrite rather than duplicating them. (7) The table must stay well-formed: every row three cells, the header row unchanged, and NO cell may contain a literal pipe character in any spelling (escaped or code-spanned) — name the matcher in prose, 'spawn_agent, alias Agent', never as a regex with an alternation bar, because the oracle's cell parser splits on pipes. (8) LEAVE ALONE the confined-writers row, which stays doctrine on Codex because karta registers no writer there, and the two rows about this repo's own execpolicy and commit gate. Also leave the earlier sentence that the behavioral gate dispatches two read-only agents exactly as written — a committed benchmarks/claims.yaml entry keys on that line — and do not introduce new numeric count claims about agents or skills anywhere in the rewrite, because the doc-truth probe's count-claim lane fails any number it has no ledger entry for. Do not touch benchmarks/flow/mutation-surface.json; its stale Codex rows are named in this binder's excluded scope as release-time bench work. SURFACING NOTE — this item is not expected to flag: it is prose about shipped behavior, with no code, no interface and no sensitive path, and the doc-truth probe checks its pointers.

oracle.command:
sh -c 'set -e; python3 - <<\PY
import re
t = open("docs/how-to/codex.md").read()
assert "## What karta enforces on Codex" in t and "### Before you rely on it" in t, "section headers moved: the parse anchors are gone"
start = t.index("## What karta enforces on Codex")
end = t.index("### Before you rely on it", start)
rows = [ln for ln in t[start:end].splitlines()
        if ln.startswith("|") and not re.match(r"^\|[-:| ]+\|$", ln)]
cells = [[c.strip() for c in ln.strip().strip("|").split("|")] for ln in rows]
assert cells and cells[0][0] == "Rule", ("parity table header not found", cells[:1])
body = cells[1:]
assert all(len(r) == 3 for r in body), ("every parity row needs three cells", [r for r in body if len(r) != 3])
codex = {r[0]: r[2] for r in body}
assert len(body) >= 11, ("the whiff row should have grown the ten-row table", len(body))
# POSITIVE CONTROL for the three absence checks below: the parse really does see
# Codex cells, and one row is still doctrine on purpose (the confined writers).
assert any("confined writers" in k.lower() and "Doctrine" in v for k, v in codex.items()), ("the confined-writers row itself must still read Doctrine", codex)
assert not any("Doctrine for now" in c for c in codex.values()), ("a dispatch row still says Doctrine for now", codex)
assert not any("Not shipped" in c for c in codex.values()), ("a row still says Not shipped", codex)
whiff = [k for k, v in codex.items() if "SubagentStop" in v]
assert len(whiff) == 1, ("expected exactly one SubagentStop row", whiff)
assert "Enforced (bundled Codex hook)" in codex[whiff[0]], ("the SubagentStop cell must itself carry the verbatim enforced label - a placeholder row cannot stand in for the whiff row", codex[whiff[0]])
auditor = [v for k, v in codex.items() if "auditor dispatch" in k.lower()]
gate = [v for k, v in codex.items() if "sized diff" in k.lower()]
assert auditor and "Enforced (bundled Codex hook)" in auditor[0], ("auditor-dispatch row not flipped to the verbatim label", auditor)
assert gate and "Enforced (bundled Codex hook)" in gate[0], ("gate-dispatch row not flipped to the verbatim label", gate)
assert "fallback" in auditor[0] and "fallback" in gate[0], ("the dispatch cells must carry the recognition-scope limit naming the generic fallback dispatch", auditor, gate)
watch = [v for k, v in codex.items() if "karta watch" in k.lower()]
assert watch and "SessionStart" in watch[0] and "--ensure" in watch[0], ("the Karta Watch row must name the SessionStart hook and keep the ensure call to action", watch)
session = [v for k, v in codex.items() if "session start" in k.lower()]
assert session and "Enforced (bundled Codex hook)" in session[0], ("session-start row not flipped to the verbatim label", session)
caveats = t[t.index("### Before you rely on it"):]
for s in ("0.124.0", "0.131.0", "[features] hooks = false", "/hooks", "hosted tools"):
    assert s in caveats, ("the GA caveat is missing " + s, s)
for s in ("Hooks may be off on your build", "behind a feature flag on some builds"):
    assert s not in t, ("the stale feature-flag caveat survives: " + s)
print("PARITY-TABLE-TRUE")
PY
grep -qF -- "SubagentStop" docs/how-to/codex.md; for gname in guard_binder_immutability.py guard_pack_write.py guard_delivery_stop.py guard_subagent_whiff.py inject_karta_status.py guard_auditor_dispatch.py guard_gate_dispatch.py; do grep -qF -- "$gname" docs/how-to/codex.md || { echo "the page never names $gname"; exit 1; }; done; python3 benchmarks/probes/parity-doc-truth-ledger.py --self-test; python3 - <<\PY
import json, subprocess
d = json.loads(subprocess.run(["python3", "benchmarks/probes/parity-doc-truth-ledger.py", "--target", "."],
                              capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout)
assert d["status"] == "pass", d
print("DOC-TRUTH-LEDGER-PASS")
PY
python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test'
assertions: the parity table is parsed cell by cell, every row carries three cells, and the ten-row table has grown to at least eleven body rows — the whiff row landed rather than replacing something

exactly one Codex cell names SubagentStop; the auditor-dispatch, gate-dispatch and session-start Codex cells each carry the verbatim 'Enforced (bundled Codex hook)' label; the two dispatch cells name the generic-fallback recognition limit; and the Karta Watch row names the SessionStart hook while keeping the --ensure call to action

no Codex cell still reads 'Doctrine for now' and none still reads 'Not shipped'; POSITIVE CONTROL for both absence assertions — the same parse must still find 'Doctrine' in the confined-writers row itself, located by its rule label, so an empty or mis-parsed table can never satisfy the absences

the caveats section states the four facts about the current hook surface: the 0.124.0 stable version, the 0.131.0 plugin-hooks version, the '[features] hooks = false' off switch, the /hooks trust review, and that hosted tools fire no hooks

the stale caveat is gone from the whole file: neither 'Hooks may be off on your build' nor 'behind a feature flag on some builds' survives anywhere in it, with the same table parse above standing as the control that the file was read

the doc-truth ledger probe passes its own hermetic --self-test and its live run over this repository returns status pass, so a broken relative link or a false count claim introduced by the rewrite is caught
validate_plugin ends in PLUGIN INTEGRITY: PASS
every bundled Codex guard script — the three existing and the four new — is named by filename somewhere on the page, checked filename by filename
